children: , the server processor and chip manufacturing company, gained renewed attention as Meta's Muse AI agent stirred interest in the chips behind AI services. Shares rose about 1.4% to $124.3095 at 10.19am ET time on Thursday. The bet is straightforward: more agents doing more tasks could mean more work for data center CPUs.

Intel has numbers to back up the demand story. In its second-quarter results, revenue climbed 25% to $16.1 billion, while Data Center and AI revenue jumped 59% to $6.3 billion. The company also launched Xeon 6+, its first server processor built on Intel 18A. Now it has to turn interest in AI agents into orders for those chips.

The valuation leaves little room for a weak follow-through. At $124.3095, Intel traded 286.78% above the $32.14 GF Value shown in the image. That gap puts the pressure on Xeon adoption, power efficiency and margins. A popular AI agent may lift demand for computing; Intel still has to prove how much of that demand it can win.

title: Intel Shares Rise as Agentic AI Keeps CPUs in the Loop
